newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-Gemina managers granted house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Gemina managers granted house arrest.

text.p: Five former managers of Italy's Gemina financial holding group held last week on suspicion of false accounting were granted house arrest on Tuesday.
The decision to release the five from prison custody was taken by judge Aurelio Barazzetta.
The five -- Emil Schneeberg, Riccardo Riccardi, Mariano Latini, Alberto Ronzoni and Felice Vitali -- were free to leave prison in Milan immediately.
Gemina's financial affairs have been under scrutiny after an investigation into alleged fraudulent book-keeping opened last year into the company and its RCS publishing division.
The company intends to hive off its industrial interests into a new company with Gemina keeping control of a few financial activities.
